already_seen_before_this_was_written: The development split's 100 draws on the base commit, summarised under development below, including every whole answer and the plan schema's reasons.
Ten further draws of one development question on a two-entity catalogue.
The client change that makes a refusal name its rule (built and tested before this record); it is part of the candidate.
The held-out questions below were written by the author of the change, after the diagnosis and before the change. No model output exists for any of them.

arms.baseline: exulanica/ at the base commit, exported unchanged with git archive and imported ahead of the worktree
arms.candidate: exulanica/ in this lane's worktree once the change is frozen. Every run records the SHA-256 of the files that decide a plan.

arms.candidate_may_not_change: what SelectionPlan accepts. Every answer either arm receives is re-validated by both arms' SelectionPlan after the run, and one disagreement fails the no_loosening gate.
arms.development_use: the change may be revised on the development split as often as needed. The held-out split sees only the frozen change.

decisions.a_no_regression_gate_fails: reported as a failure, with the questions that moved
decisions.all_gates_pass: the change is this lane's result and goes to root with these numbers
decisions.baseline_place_rate_at_least_6000_bp: the held-out split did not reproduce the defect, so no improvement is claimed from it, whatever the candidate scores
decisions.latency_or_cost_fails: reported as a failure of that gate; the rates are still reported
decisions.no_loosening_fails: the change is withdrawn: it passed by accepting plans the base commit refuses
decisions.place_rate_or_improvement_fails: reported as a failure. The held-out split is not used to revise the change. Root decides whether a partial improvement is worth taking.
decisions.provider_errors_over_10_percent_of_an_ar: the run is void and is reported as void, not scored

definitions.cost: provider-reported tokens times the manifest's listed prices, every attempt included
definitions.intents: captures and entities resolve the same photographs and give the composer the same packet, so a question about what photographs show accepts either. content is the cross-content listing and is right only for an explicit request for related material.
definitions.latency: wall milliseconds of one propose_plan call, repair included
definitions.query_rule: a null query passes when the question allows null. A query passes when it has at least one word after stop words, every word is in the question's allowed list, and, when the question names required words, at least one of them is present. Words are lowercase letter runs, plural-folded by the scorer's stem function.
definitions.rate: right draws over draws, per kind. A draw ending in a provider error (not a refusal) is excluded and counted separately.
definitions.right_plan: the planner returned a plan (no refusal after its repair), every id in it is in the catalogue with a place selector holding places only, and it is the plan the question asks for: an accepted intent, exactly the expected place and entity ids, an accepted entity mode and content scope, no time window, no capture property, epistemic confirmed, and a semantic query allowed by the question's query rule

not_covered: Whether the right plan finds the right photograph: retrieval, the text join and the packet are not exercised. Only the plan is scored.
The plan's limit is not scored, so a right plan with a null query and a limit of one may still hand the composer the wrong photograph at a place with several.

record.premise: MEASURED on the development split, base commit, 100 draws: place questions about something visible or written there were refused 20 of 20. Every first attempt chose intent content with content scope memories_only and a semantic query, which SelectionPlan refuses ('cross-content place membership is relational and does not use semantic text'), and every repair returned the same plan: the refusal the repair carried quoted the answer and never named the rule. Without a place the same pull appears (a sign question chose content on 5 of 5 first attempts) and the repair recovers it. 'Who was with me at' a place put an unnamed person into the entity filter 5 of 5 times. Person questions were right 30 of 30 and plain content questions 30 of 30.

procedure.cap_usd_per_run: 0.50, stated in the environment and on the command line
procedure.order: ten runs of one draw of every held-out question, alternating baseline and candidate, baseline first, so the two arms share the provider's conditions

record.profile_note: Pre-registration of the Companion planner reliability experiment. Written after the development diagnosis and before any change to the planner's prompt, plan validation or repair; no model has been sent any held-out question.
record.question: Does a change to the planner make it return the right plan for worded questions about a place, without making person or plain content questions worse, within a latency and cost ceiling?
